newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ten killed in rebel raids in Algeria, newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed in rebel raids in Algeria, newspaper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem guerrillas shot dead ten Algerians in two separate attacks, including three Moslem worshippers killed inside a mosque, an Algerian newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The Arabic-language daily al Khabar said Moslem rebels shot and killed seven ceramic workers on Monday in the northeastern town of Tidjelabine, some 40 km (25 miles) east of Algiers.

Gunmen, believed to be Moslem rebels, broke into a mosque packed with worshippers during last Friday prayers and gunned down three people in the small town of Hasnaoua in the eastern province of Boumerdes, 50 km (31 miles) from Algiers, it added.

On Tuesday night, a huge explosion rocked the Frais Valon district which overlooks the Moslem fundamentalist stronghold of Bab el Oued in central Algiers, causing panic among residents in neighbouring suburbs, Liberte newspaper said on Wednesday.
The newspaper did not say whether there was any casualty from the explosion which it described as of "huge intensity".
The Algerian authorities, stepping up campaign across the country to rally voters support for the 28 November referendum to change the constitution, made no statement on the incidents.
Around 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists were set to win.
